[re: Great Beast or Huitzilopochtli with Ex Nihilo, Meat Hook, Fear of
the Void Below, Trap, Thoughts Betrayed, for infinite-library-discardage]

> > Would need something to set range to close first. A small Nos to enable
> > you to play Storm Sewers for example.

> discard a card from the opposing minion's hand. I think the meathook is
> just there to provide an extra press. The goal, of course, is to keep
> going and eventually discard the opponents entire library and hand.
> Technically, with the right draw and enough presses, this would be
possible.
> Why not just stack multiple traps? Would do just the same I'd
> imagine...sure, you have to play them on the first round of combat...but
> still....finding two presses to end when you're randomly discarding a card
> from your hand each round could be tough.

Well, the goal is to deplete any player's library in a single combat.
With just Trap (no matter how many of them you play) you can't go
over 4 rounds (and therefore 4 forced discards). The Meat Hooks are
supposed to make combat last indefinitely (since with Ex Nihilo the
Meat Hook strikes aren't inflicting damage but are giving presses),
but the problem then is that Fear of the Void Below defaults range
to long and there's no good way to get to close each round (that I
can see - Cailean, yes, but him getting those disciplines adds all
kinds of moving parts to the concept).

If you work in a card that can be played to extend Trap-time, you
can make the combat last as long as you can keep drawing that card,
but you then burn 1/4 as many cards as your opponent does, so you'll
probably eventually run out yourself and be somewhat less able to
gain advantage from having run people out of cards.

Josh

Messages.Author: Creature
Messages.Body:
I think what this thread is looking for is the fact that trap states
that "During the press step, if any Methuselah has played a card
earlier in the current round or during the two previous rounds, the
Trap automatically provides a press to continue (either combatant can
press to end)."

The combo is not destructive since cards have to be played, and not
discarded. A discard does not count as a played card, therefore combat
does not continue indefinitely, and the combo cannot deplete the
entire library in one combat.

Does this make any sense?

Messages.Author: Rafe
Messages.Body:
> But, forgive me if I missed something, but there is no way to prevent a
> vampire with potence to break the Meat Hook, right?

Yes, there are ways to prevent the potence-possessing vampire from
destroying the meathook. Assuming they have been successful in
entering combat and are at close range (e.g. they have not been
Obedienced or the opposing vampire has not set range to long somehow
or outmaneuvered them to long) a Strike: Combat Ends or Strike: Dodge
will prevent them from destroying the Meat Hook as either will take
effect before First Strike.

An Immortal Grapple will also prevent them from attempting the strike
to destroy the Meat Hook in the first place, as the strike to destroy
the Meat Hook does not qualify as a hand strike ("any non-ranged,
non-weapon strike that deals damage based on the striking minion's
strength, or any minion's non-ranged damage-dealing innate strike").

- Rafe
